rows.description: A young child greets with namaste, salaam, a bow or a blessing sign as taught. These greetings show respect and belonging, and forms vary by family, region and faith.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler recites a short prayer or asks for blessings, or says thanks before a meal. Meaning is learned through routine and warmth, and the child can ask simple questions about what it means.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child reads raised brows for questions or mouth shapes that modify signs. In signed languages, facial and body movements are grammatical and not just emotion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young signer learns handshapes, locations and movements that make up signs, as spoken children learn sounds. Signed languages have their own grammar, not simplified gestures.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Drawing and early writing of messages [Expressing]
rows.description: A preschooler draws and scribbles "letters" to share feelings, such as a card for a parent. The message lies in the intent and picture, and adults respond to the meaning rather than the spelling.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Dramatic play and acting out roles [Expressing]
rows.description: A preschooler plays doctor, parent or monster with voices and gestures, working through fears and everyday events. Scary play is often a way to master worry rather than a sign of wrongdoing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child tells a story with puppets, giving characters feelings the child may not yet name directly. A wise listener asks about the character first, without pressing the child to admit the story is about them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child draws a house, sun and family, often with bright colours for what feels important. A drawing is a starting point for conversation, and colour or size alone should not be over-interpreted as a diagnosis.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler presses a drawing or a rakhi into an adult's hand, expressing affection, wish to please or gratitude. Receiving it warmly teaches that feelings can be shared through objects.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler wears a cape, a saree or a uniform of a favourite job, trying on who they might be. Dress-up is imaginative play, and it does not fix identity for the future.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
